title: Surfacing brain stimulation.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC core record (open access = N, in PMC = N, has supplementary = N, has data = N, no text-mined accessions), Crossref metadata (single page 471-471, single author Jianxun Ren, 15 references), a Zenodo search on the DOI (0 hits), and the publisher page (HTTP 403, subscription required). No data file of any kind is attached or linked.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Only the one-sentence abstract, 'Brain functional circuits can guide precision surface brain stimulation', plus a web summary saying the piece argues for moving neuromodulation from deep implanted electrodes to functional circuits reachable at the brain surface. No methods, no results, no cohort, no numbers were retrievable.

a1_downloadable.note: There is no dataset. This is a one-page, single-author Science essay/commentary (page 471-471, 15 references) with no supplementary files, no accessions, no repository deposit, and the full text itself is behind a subscription (publisher page returned HTTP 403).

plain_idea.one_liner: Use each person's brain-connectivity map to predict the best scalp or surface site to stimulate for symptom relief.
plain_idea.train_on: Would need per-patient resting-state functional MRI (magnetic resonance imaging taken while the person lies still, showing which brain regions fluctuate together) plus the stimulation site and dose actually delivered. This essay supplies zero such examples.
plain_idea.predict: Change in a clinical rating scale (for example motor score in Parkinson's disease) after stimulation, measured by a clinician before and after treatment. No such outcome table is attached here.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Clinicians choosing a non-invasive stimulation target currently rely on group-average atlases; a personalised target predictor could raise response rates. But this paper provides no data to build it from.

ml_idea: The topic (individualised, connectivity-guided brain stimulation targets) is a real machine-learning opportunity, but it would have to be built from other sources entirely: for example the Human Connectome Project or UK Biobank imaging for connectivity, plus a public transcranial magnetic stimulation outcome cohort. None of that comes from this paper, so this is not a candidate.
